claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC alloy.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Mechanical alloying followed by consolidation such as spark plasma sintering can incorporate Y2O3 into TiVNbTa.
The proposed processing will produce nanometer-scale, uniformly distributed Y2O3 dispersoids within the BCC matrix.
The Y2O3 dispersoids will remain stable under elevated-temperature service.
Finely dispersed Y2O3 particles impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Finely dispersed Y2O3 particles impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will retard creep and high-temperature softening.
Oxide-dispersion strengthening is widely applied in refractory and high-temperature materials to delay deformation.
Introducing well-distributed Y2O3 dispersoids will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength above the 330 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will retain ductility suitable for use as a W/CuCrZr heat-transfer interlayer.
The proposed intervention is intended to operate at temperatures up to approximately 1273 K under loading relevant to W/CuCrZr heat-transfer interlayers.
